```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The `embt` package tests whether two outcome distributions differ only by a
location shift. The null can be written as constancy of the expectile treatment
effect over a prespecified range of expectile indices.

## A two-sample test

The treatment variable must be binary. Numeric treatment variables use zero
for control and one for treatment. For factors, the first level is control and
the second level is treatment.

```{r}
library(embt)

set.seed(2026)
n <- 120
experiment <- data.frame(
  treatment = rep(0:1, each = n / 2),
  baseline = rnorm(n)
)
experiment$outcome <- 1 + experiment$treatment +
  (1 + 0.25 * experiment$treatment) * rnorm(n) +
  0.5 * experiment$baseline

set.seed(11)
fit <- embt(outcome ~ treatment, data = experiment, B = 99)
summary(fit)
```

The summary reports four tests. `S-KS` and `S-CvM` use the regular-process
studentization that remains well defined at the mean coordinate.

## Fixed-basis covariate adjustment

```{r}
set.seed(11)
fit_ca <- embt(
  outcome ~ treatment,
  data = experiment,
  adjust = ~ baseline,
  B = 99
)
summary(fit_ca)
```

Covariates must be measured before treatment assignment, and the adjustment
basis should be prespecified. The basis dimension is fixed; the procedure does
not select a bandwidth or fit a nonparametric nuisance function.

## Process estimates

The estimated centered expectile treatment-effect curve is available in the
`process` component and can be plotted directly.

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
plot(fit_ca, version = "both")
```

A raw KS simultaneous confidence band can be requested with:

```{r}
head(confint(fit_ca, parm = "adjusted"))
```
